prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “best” roofing company for everyone — the best roofer for you depends on your location in Dallas, roof type, budget, whether you’re filing an insurance claim, and what warranties/certifications you want. I can help you pick one once you tell me a bit more. Meanwhile, here’s how to find the best contractor and what to look for.

What to tell me so I can make specific recommendations
- Are you in the City of Dallas or somewhere in the DFW suburbs?  
- Residential or commercial roof replacement?  
- Roof material (asphalt shingles, metal, tile, flat/torch-down)?  
- Are you filing an insurance claim?  
- Any deadline or HOA requirements?

How to choose the best Dallas roofing company
1. Get at least 3 written estimates that include materials, scope, timeline, cleanup, and permits.  
2. Look for manufacturer certifications — e.g., GAF Master Elite, Owens Corning Preferred, CertainTeed Select ShingleMaster. These mean the contractor meets training/insurance criteria and offers stronger warranties.  
3. Verify insurance and licensing — ask for general liability and workers’ comp policy numbers and call the carrier to confirm coverage. Confirm they will pull required city permits.  
4. Check reputation — search Google/Yelp/Angi/HomeAdvisor and the BBB for ratings and complaints; ask for local references and recent photos of completed jobs.  
5. Warranties — get both manufacturer and workmanship warranty in writing (length and what’s covered). Know who you call if problems arise.  
6. Written contract — don’t pay large upfront sums; avoid contractors insisting on cash-only deals. The contract should list materials, payment schedule, start/finish dates, and cleanup/disposal.  
7. Storm-chaser warning — don’t hire contractors who just appeared after a storm without local references or an office/phone you can verify.

Key questions to ask each roofer
- Are you licensed/registered for work in Texas? Can you provide proof?  
- Do you carry general liability and workers’ comp? Can I have the policy info?  
- Are you a certified installer for the shingle brand I want? What warranties are offered?  
- Will you handle city permits and inspections?  
- Do you provide a written contract and final invoice?  
- Can you show recent local projects and references?

Red flags
- No physical address or only a PO box.  
- Requests for full payment upfront or cash-only deals.  
- High-pressure “today only” discounts or going door-to-door after a storm.  
- Unwillingness to provide proof of insurance or references.

How I can help next
- If you give me your neighborhood and roof type, I can suggest several well-reviewed Dallas-area roofing contractors to contact and list what to ask each.  
- Or paste 2–3 estimates you received and I’ll help compare them line-by-line.

Would you like contractor suggestions for your area? If so tell me city/neighborhood and whether it’s a shingle or other roof.
